Titus Aelius Rufus stands near the muddy water's edge, a bent iron nail held between his thumb and forefinger. He taps it against his front teeth, then holds it up so the morning light catches the dull metal.

"May Vulcan see that no man is lost to the river," he says, his voice flat and low. "You wear the clothes of no trade I know. You are not a soldier, and your hair is cut short and even. You are not a Greek. Your skin is pale, but you do not burn in the sun as a Greek would. Where do you come from, and what is your craft?"

His eyes do not blink. They move slowly over your filthy t-shirt and the torn jeans, lingering on the OtterBox in your pocket.

Livia Aelia stands behind him, her fingers counting the folds of her woolen palla. She watches the stranger's face, her gaze soft and searching.
